questions.learningObjective: Define and distinguish key film studies concepts
questions.stem: Which statement best defines Point of view?

options.text: It is the perspective through which the story is filtered and presented to the audience.
It is a narrator whose account is partial, biased, or outright false.
options.misconception: Confuses Point of view with Unreliable narrator

options.text: It is a narrative voice that knows the private thoughts of all the characters.
options.misconception: Confuses Point of view with Omniscient narrator

options.text: It is the perspective through which the narrative information is selected and coloured.
options.misconception: mixes up Point of view with Focalisation

questions.explanation: It is the perspective through which the story is filtered and presented to the audience. This is precisely what Point of view means. Option B ("It is a narrator whose account is partial, biased, or outright…") is wrong because it confuses Point of view with Unreliable narrator; Option C ("It is a narrative voice that knows the private thoughts of all…") is wrong because it confuses Point of view with Omniscient narrator; Option D ("It is the perspective through which the narrative information i…") is wrong because it mixes up Point of view with Focalisation.
questions.hint: Recall the specific meaning of Point of view.
